Tried this game despite the bad reviews because I wanted something to scratch that looter shooter itch, and I was blown away...by how remarkably bland it was.

 Like, genuinely, they are clearly trying to make something inspired by Destiny and Warframe and really just fail at capturing the appeal of either. The gameplay is mushy and boring, the shooting is bland, the enemies are slow and predictable, at no point in my 2.7 hours of play did I feel challenged in any fashion and mostly just stood in the open clicking heads.

The loot was bland and uninteresting, the weapons just looking for higher numbers to replace what I currently had. They had some module system clearly inspired by the mods in Warframe but they did nothing interesting and didn't alter gameplay in any fashion besides making numbers go higher.

 Also, for a modern 'AAA' game, it looks like complete trash, like genuinely there are PS3 games that look better. All the graphics are mushy and the antialiasing seems trash.

All in all, this game will be quickly forgotten.

The micro-transactions are arranged to greatly improve inventory space, customizations, and most of all: bypass large material grinds.  I myself dont mind paying for convenience, but if you intend to play this game for free, you will need to be very patient and enjoy the process of grinding.  The gunplay is fun, the mod system is similar to Warframe and is a nice system for making builds: defensive vs offensive, firearms vs skills, mobility or utility.  The skills range from critically essential, to somewhat useless.  I really like the various world zones: small buildings, industrial facilities, swamps, forest, snowy mountains, and a heavy focus on desert.  Expect to periodically get stuck at story bosses and need to grind for mods, materials, and gear to become powerful enough.  Also, die a lot and learn.  You only lose some time invested on each attempt, no permanent punishments for death.

The game isn't actually that bad. Story line is fully free, 95 % of content absolutely free. Shooting feels comfortable, game play is laid-back, especially as Ajax until you hit the Pyromaniac arc. There are plenty of well-fitted girls in latex suits, giving the game a chilled vibe. The mobility is impressive, allowing for crazy movement with double jumps, grappling hooks, and well-implemented skills. There's no pay-to-win aspect either.

However, you'll encounter repetition with heroes in identical suits and skills. Customized items require purchasing skins, and custom painting isn't allowed.

The story feels lackluster (though who really cares when there are attractive characters on screen), seeming effortless and almost AI-generated, like a 'cool future' story pitting an old, bulky steroid guy against the Powerpuff Girls.

The game heavily emphasizes grinding, which I don't mind, but it demands a lot of time and can feel empty at times. Unlike games like Diablo 4, where grinding feels rewarding with higher world levels and noticeable progress in damage, this game didn't give me the same satisfaction.
6 out of 10.

Misc newbie tips: Map Screen > Access Info will help with most "wtf is this?" questions (also best way to track specific ingredients and how to source them) // Searching ingredients after speaking with Anais will show you what craftables use it. // Get Sharen ASAP so you can get bonus materials with successful infiltrations. // For PC: To access the main map, 'M' to access the local map and 'G' for the global map (vs running to the terminal each time) // Currently the best way to level up Descendants is by running the wave defense missions ("Special Operations") in Kingston and the Echo Swamp // Learn how to use the item filter to help quickly get rid of lowest ranking gear ("Filter all as Junk") // There are a few confusing function labels - "Register Attached Items" means "Favorite" // Modules assigned to weapons are not bound to the weapons (so when you recycle the weapon, you keep the modules automatically). // Once you figure out what Amorpheous Materials are used for & how to get/open them, the colossus battles are pretty fun. The Dead Bride is the first significant hurdle that might set you back to rethink your build // There are a few critical questions that can be answered by continuing to play the main quest line - otherwise use Google to search reddit for specific questions.
